title: Bonsai Batcher: span-pruner runtime for sequence bucketing and pad reduction
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight runtime component ("Bonsai Batcher") that performs dynamic sequence-length bucketing and aggressive padding pruning at the micro-batch boundary with kernel-affinity hints for the scheduler. The goal is to reduce wasted padding tokens across mixed-sequence workloads while keeping p95 decode latency regression under 5% and improving end-to-end token throughput for typical web-chat workloads.

Background: We observe high padding overhead when many short requests are coalesced with a few long ones. Existing bucketers are either heavy-weight (global re-bucketing) or static (fixed-length bins). Bonsai Batcher is an incremental, low-latency shaper inserted between the request coalescer and the kernel scheduler that performs: (1) span-pruning: selective tail-trimming for prefills based on probabilistic attention window preservation, (2) radius bucketing: continuous bins with soft boundaries to allow small sequence-length differences to be coalesced, and (3) kernel hints: emit per-microbatch kernel-affinity metadata (preferred kernel, quantization profile) for faster kernel selection.

Why unique: Uses a two-pass prefill steering flow (quick heuristic pass that trims obvious pad + a second low-overhead verification pass that ensures no quality regressions for prompts flagged as sensitive). Adds an empirical pad budget allocator so long-tail requests can borrow budget from near-term short requests for better throughput without violating per-request SLOs.

Success metrics (quantitative targets):
- Padding tokens reduced by >= 25% on internal mixed-seq benchmark (chat-short + doc-long).
- End-to-end token throughput +7% to +12% on RTX-8000 cluster tests.
- p95 decode latency change <= +5% vs baseline (no shaper) with target 99th percentile tails unaffected by >10%.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests show pad token reduction >= 20% on three canonical workload traces
Unit tests for span-pruner heuristics with deterministic seeds
CI e2e benchmark job demonstrates no more than +5% p95 latency delta on decoding-heavy workload
Kernel-affinity header produced and validated by kernel scheduler simulator
technical_design:
Architecture: Bonsai lives in the serving runtime pipeline after request coalescer and before kernel scheduler. Implementation is ~500 LOC Rust component with small C++ shim for tight kernel metadata structs. Components: 1) Fast estimator: computes a lightweight score for each request (entropy proxy + recent prefix growth) to decide safe trim length. 2) Span-pruner: applies probabilistic tail trimming using attention-preservation mask heuristics. 3) Radius bucketer: groups requests into soft bins using an L1-distance metric with tunable radius. 4) Budget allocator: per-microbatch pad budget reconciler with borrow/repay semantics. 5) Kernel hint emitter: attach "k_affinity" and "quant_profile" tags to microbatch for scheduler optimization.

Algorithm notes: The estimator uses a tiny sampled-prefix-perplexity proxy (3-token ngram) to avoid invoking the model. Span-pruner uses a rolling attention-cost estimate: if estimated attention cost of tail tokens < theta, trim up to R tokens. Radius bucketer uses exponential decay weighting to prefer coalescing sequences with close lengths without large variance. Budget allocator enforces per-request minimums to avoid starving long sequences.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive trimming reduces cost but can change output for generative continuations. We mitigate with two-pass verification: mark requests with "sensitive_output" label (from client metadata) and only apply conservative trimming. We chose a low-memory estimator to avoid additional KV cache pressure. Kernel hints add metadata overhead (~12 bytes/microbatch) but allow up to 6-8% faster kernel selection in the scheduler throughput tests.
implementation_notes: Step 1: Implement estimator + unit tests (owner: Marco)
Step 2: Span-pruner with deterministic seedable randomness for tests
Step 3: Integrate radius bucketer into coalescer pipeline and emit k_affinity tags
Step 4: Add microbench harness to measure pad tokens and latency on staging cluster
Step 5: Run canary against small percentage of traffic (10%) with fallbacks
test_plan: Baseline run: existing coalescer without Bonsai on mixed-seq trace (3 runs median)
Feature-on run: Bonsai enabled with default config (3 runs median)
A/B validation: compare token cost, p95 and p99 latency, and output diffs using eval prompts
Regression tests for KV cache correctness after trimming (no cache poison)
Fuzz tests for radius bucketer boundaries and budget allocator overflow
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - internal perf tests only (dev cluster)
Stage 2 - Canary: 10% of hosted API traffic, monitor cost and latencies for 48h
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: 30% -> 60% -> full in 4-day increments if metrics pass
Fallback: automatic disable on >7% p95 regression or >5% customer error increase
monitoring_alerts: Alert if p95_decode_latency increases >7% sustained over 10m
Alert if kernel_mismatch_rate > 2% (hints rejected by scheduler)
